title: Single-pulse strain-induced precessional dynamics of magnetization in Co-doped iron garnet
authors: Héloïse Damas, Carl S. Davies, Tomasz Zalewski, Petr M. Vetoshko, Vladimir I. Belotelov, Andrzej Stupakiewicz, Andrei Kirilyuk
abstract: Ultrafast control of magnetization through lattice excitation provides a route to manipulating magnetic order on short timescales, yet the role of transient strain in driving magnetization dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, single-shot pump-probe magneto-optical microscopy is used to resolve the structural and magnetic responses of cobalt-doped yttrium iron garnet to individual 5-ps mid-infrared pulses. The excitation generates a localized strain field together with an outward-propagating elastic wave. Concurrently, the magnetic contrast decreases following excitation and subsequently reverses on a timescale of approximately 1.5-2 ns before recovering to its initial state. The structural and magnetic responses exhibit closely correlated wavelength and pulse-energy dependences, indicating a common excitation pathway. Micromagnetic simulations incorporating transient strain reproduce the precessional reorientation of the magnetization within individual domains while largely preserving the labyrinthine domain morphology. These results identify transient lattice deformation as the link between single-pulse mid-infrared excitation and reversible precessional magnetization dynamics in Co-doped yttrium iron garnet.
summary: This paper investigates how ultrafast mid-infrared pulses control magnetization in Co-doped yttrium iron garnet. By combining single-shot pump-probe microscopy with micromagnetic simulations, the authors demonstrate that the excitation generates a transient strain field. This lattice deformation is identified as the crucial link responsible for driving the reversible, precessional dynamics of the magnetization.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the precise role of transient lattice strain in driving and mediating the magnetization dynamics of magnetic garnets following ultrafast, single-pulse mid-infrared excitation.
main_result: The research establishes that transient lattice deformation acts as the direct physical link connecting the single-pulse excitation to the observed reversible precessional reorientation of magnetization in Co-doped yttrium iron garnet.
method: The work combines single-shot pump-probe magneto-optical microscopy to measure time-resolved magnetic and structural responses with micromagnetic simulations incorporating transient strain effects.
model_or_system: The physical system is Cobalt-doped yttrium iron garnet (Co:YIG). The dynamics are modeled using micromagnetic simulations (MuMax3) that incorporate the coupling between the magnetic order and the transient strain field generated by the excitation pulse.
key_observables: Time-resolved magnetic contrast (showing decrease, reversal at $\approx 1.5-2$ ns, and recovery), localized strain field (four-lobe symmetry), and the resulting precessional reorientation of magnetization.
important_parameters: Excitation pulse duration (5-ps), excitation wavelength ($\lambda$: 8 to 22 $\mu$m), and the timescale of magnetization reversal ($\approx 1.5-2$ ns).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the structural and magnetic responses are coupled via the transient strain field, and that the single-pulse excitation isolates this specific magnetoelastic pathway.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the initial labyrinthine domain structure and the transient magnetic response; other figures show the localized strain response (four-lobe pattern) and compare the correlated time-evolution of magnetic contrast and strain signals.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the problem of strain's role in ultrafast dynamics. It then presents experimental results using single-shot pump-probe techniques to measure correlated structural and magnetic changes. Finally, micromagnetic simulations are employed to reproduce the observed precessional dynamics, confirming the strain-mediated mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a clear, experimentally verified mechanism (strain mediation) for controlling magnetic dynamics using optical excitation, which is highly relevant for developing ultrafast spintronic devices and understanding light-matter interactions in magnetic insulators.
